table: Figure 11 (review volume, pre-monetization giveaways); simple aggregate printed in results/demand/demand-log.txt
replication_status: exact (did::att_gt with the authors' settings reproduces the authors' simple aggregate 5.7462 (0.1294), which equals the printed 5.75 to the printed decimals; verified against the article Nov 4 2026)
notes: Authors' did::att_gt(yname N, tname ym_num, idname focal_book_id, gname giveaways_ym_num, control_group nevertreated, anticipation 1, allow_unbalanced_panel TRUE, clustervar focal_book_id) on pre-monetization giveaway books (giveaway before Jan 2018) plus one Goodreads 'similar' never-giveaway book per focal book (gname 0, id = focal id*10+1), +/-12 months around the focal giveaway month (code/code-raw-data/demand_data_cleaning_code.R line 301). Panel extracted from the shipped fitted object vol_premon_attgt_similarcontrol.gz (DIDparams$data): 2,934,550 book-months, 117,382 ids (58,691 treated + 58,691 never-treated), 24 cohorts, 48 periods, balanced 25 rows per unit. Re-aggregating the shipped object reproduces 5.74625 (analytic SE 0.1222; the authors' 0.1294 is a bootstrap SE). gvar = giveaway month, so the giveaway month is the first treated period as in the authors' did call; the pipeline cannot represent anticipation = 1 (deviation). Control group is a chosen similar-books set, not statistical matching. AUTHORS' CSA SETTINGS (PROTOCOL 5b Hull alignment (c), Nov 2; demand_data_cleaning_code.R lines 301-376, 02_demand_results.R lines 400-457): did::att_gt(control_group = 'nevertreated', allow_unbalanced_panel = TRUE, est_method dr, base_period varying, anticipation = 1), aggte(type = 'simple', na.rm = TRUE). csa_control_group = 'nevertreated'. anticipation = 1 means the base period is g-2 and the anticipation month g-1 of treated books is used neither as a pre nor a post period. It is represented without a new field: data file *_panel_ant.rds (prepared copy, prep_anticipation.R in the same folder) adds g_ant = giveaway month - 1 and ant_row = treated book-month at giveaway month - 1; gvar = g_ant and sample_filter ant_row == 0. The (g_ant, g_ant) cell is then empty (dropped by aggte na.rm), the base period is g_ant - 1 = g-2 and the post cells start at the giveaway month, so the simple ATT equals the authors' (checked). The same rows are dropped for TWFE and BJS (PROTOCOL (c)); on the retained rows the TWFE indicator is 1[month >= giveaway month]. Superseded: the earlier note that anticipation = 1 is not representable. Hull default (not-yet-treated, no anticipation) on the original panel gives 1.2758. TIMING: the paper's TWFE (Table 4, spec T4vol_c2_post_giveaway) starts treatment the month AFTER the giveaway (post_giveaway = 1(yearmon > giveaway_yearmon)), whereas the CSA (gname = giveaway month) treats the giveaway month as the first treated period; this spec's constructed TWFE follows the CSA timing, so it is not comparable to the published Table 4 TWFE.
published_source: Printed in Section 4.5.1 of the published article (papers/mnsc/mnsc.2023.01390.pdf): 'The overall treatment effect of Giveaway participation on number of ratings is 5.75 ... and 15.53', no SE printed; read Nov 4 2026; equals the authors' simple aggregate 5.7462 (0.1294) in results/demand/demand-log.txt to the printed decimals (authors_code_*). Earlier: Article (Management Science 72(3), 2026) Section 4.5.1: 'The overall treatment effect of Giveaway participation on number of ratings is 5.75 for the pre-monetization sample, compared with 15.53 for the postmonetization sample'; Figure 11 plots the dynamic ATTs. published_coef/se (5.7462, bootstrap 0.1294) are the authors' printed simple aggregate in results/demand/demand-log.txt, which rounds to the text value.
csa_weights_note: Nov 2: the published CSA comes from R did (or staggered, whose estimates did reproduces), which weights cells by fixed cohort shares; Hull's DiD-averaging weights cells by treated-observation counts. 'did' reproduces the published number (main analysis, option B); the strict-Hull run (CSA_STRICT_HULL=1, option A) ignores this field.
